chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Recording with Thomas Morris in 1926
summary: Caldwell recalls Thomas Morris, uncle of Marlowe Morris, the 1926 electrical recordings and Morris's later turn to Father Divine's church.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well now, let me see. We're up to Johnny Johnson. We have -- oh, when you -- you made some records with Thomas Morris.
Tommy Morris in 1926.
Well, who was he?
He was a nice trumpet player. Marlowe Marlon Morris, the piano player -- you've heard of him.
Yeah, I know who he is.
That's his uncle.
Oh, yes. Yes.

That's his uncle. We made those records in 1926, first orthophonic recordings, electrical recordings. Tommy -- later on, around about the early '30's, about the middle '30's, he joined Father Divine's church.
Oh, I wondered what happened to him.
That's what happened to him.
(unintelligible) musician, huh?
Yeah, played trumpet with Father Divine's church.
Yeah, because he made records (unintelligible) with Pats Waller on organ (unintelligible).
That's right. Yeah. That's right.
Well, that was -- for those records you made, though, with Bernie.
With Bernie.
And you made these for RCA?
Yeah.
And that was the second lot, wasn't it?
That was the second lot.
